Do NOT silently leave an unchecked AC."},{"id":"CG-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"The check-invocation-log-entry.sh onboarded-operator-bump STATUS.md regex uses an anchored bullet-format prefix (^- \*\*TF-024X-renovate-...) that is more restrictive than the plan-doc file-agnostic spec regex (TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-...). The plan-doc §2 invariant 2 explicitly states 'The regex is file-agnostic: it matches the TF reference content, not the surrounding markdown (so the same line passes whether it has a - **...** STATUS.md bullet wrapper, lives in a DISPATCH-NOTE prose paragraph, or is otherwise embedded)'.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 192-196: pattern = rf'(?m)^- \*\*TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{{19,}}$' — requires start-of-line + '- **' prefix. Plan-doc §2 invariant 2 canonical regex: 'TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}' — no line-start anchor, no prefix. Compare: blocked-on-adopter-conflict path (lines 207-210) correctly uses an unanchored search: pattern = rf'TF-024X-conflict-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{{19,}}'. The two paths use asymmetric patterns despite the spec describing a single file-agnostic regex for both.","impact":"A STATUS.md TF row written as plain prose (without the '- **...**' bullet format) would pass the plan-doc spec but fail the CI check. While in practice all STATUS.md TF rows use the bullet format, the implementation diverges from the stated spec principle and creates a latent bypass vector: an operator who writes the TF row differently (e.g., inside a table or prose paragraph in STATUS.md) would get a false-failure from the CI gate.","mitigation":"Update the onboarded-operator-bump pattern to match the plan-doc file-agnostic spec: use re.search with the unanchored pattern 'TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}' (no ^-\*\* prefix, no $ end-anchor). Add a test case that verifies a plain-prose STATUS.md TF entry (without bullet) also passes."},{"id":"CG-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"The restore_branch_protection() function in enable-required-check.sh emits a log entry where both the 'PUT payload applied' and 'Before' blocks show restore_before_json (the target state being restored to), rather than 'Before' showing the current branch-protection state before the restore PUT was applied. This breaks the log entry convention (Before = state before this operation) and would confuse an auditor reviewing the log.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh lines 347-379: restore_before_json is used for both the PUT payload and the Before block. The '- **Before:**' section at line 369 prints 'restore_before_json' (same JSON as the PUT payload applied). The '- **After:**' section at line 373 correctly prints restore_after_json. The restore function fetches current state only at line 339 (restore_after_json) which is AFTER the PUT, not before it. There is no capture of the current state before the restore PUT is applied (no pre-restore GET).","impact":"Audit trail ambiguity: a reviewer reading the log entry sees Before = PUT payload (i.e., target state) and After = actual post-restore state. Typically Before should show what was changed from. Without a pre-restore GET, the log entry does not show what branch-protection state was active on the target repo at the moment the restore ran. For the D-035 audit trail to be complete, the log must show the state being overwritten, not the state being restored to.","mitigation":"Add a pre-restore GET before the PUT in restore_branch_protection(): capture current state as CURRENT_JSON, use it in the 'Before' block. The PUT payload block already shows what is being applied (restore_before_json); Before should show what is being replaced (CURRENT_JSON). This makes the log entry unambiguous: Before = live state before restore, After = live state after restore, PUT payload = the target we restored to."},{"id":"CG-MIN-003","severity":"MIN","claim":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh exercises only the --diff-base mode. The --pr mode (gh pr diff) is entirely untested. Additionally, the parse_entry_repo function in --pr mode receives a full-PR diff (all files) rather than a file-scoped diff, creating a latent correctness issue where a '+### heading — something@something' line in any other changed file could be misread as a log entry target.","evidence":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh line 52-53: every run_case call uses '--diff-base base', no test uses '--pr'. check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 142-148: --pr path uses 'gh pr diff PR --name-only' and 'gh pr diff PR --patch' (full PR diff); --diff-base path uses 'git diff --name-only' and 'git diff -- BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG' (file-scoped). parse_entry_repo() iterates ALL '+### ' lines in the patch, which in --pr mode spans all changed files.","impact":"In CI where --pr mode would be the natural invocation, untested code paths run. The parse_entry_repo latent bug means a PR that changes any documentation file containing a level-3 heading followed by ' — owner/repo@branch' could have its log-entry target misidentified, causing a false-pass for cascade-status=onboarded.","mitigation":"Add at least one positive and one negative test case that exercises --pr mode (can be mocked with a local git repo + stub gh binary). Fix parse_entry_repo to filter the patch to the branch-protection-log file section before iterating: in --pr mode, use 'gh pr diff PR --patch -- BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG' (pass the path restriction to gh pr diff)."},{"id":"CG-MIN-004","severity":"MIN","claim":"VERSIONING.md's 'branch-protection helper' breaking-change enumeration lists only the original enable-required-check.sh flags (--repo, --branch, --plan, --no-enforce-admins, --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate). The two new flags added by slice 024B (--restore and --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci) are not enumerated. Future removal of these flags would not be flagged as a breaking change under the current VERSIONING.md contract.","evidence":"policies/VERSIONING.md §'Branch-protection helper': 'Removing --repo, --branch, --plan, --no-enforce-admins, or --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate flags from scripts/enable-required-check.sh.' D-044 row in DECISIONS.md mentions '--restore mode' and '--i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci flag' as newly adopted operational contracts.","impact":"If a future slice removes --restore (e.g., replacing it with a different restore mechanism), the VERSIONING.md contract does not require a MAJOR bump or a deprecation-ramp entry. Adopters relying on --restore for their break-glass procedure (per ADOPT-001 §12.8) could find the flag silently removed without the one-release warning window the contract promises for breaking changes.","mitigation":"Update policies/VERSIONING.md §'Branch-protection helper' breaking-change row to include: 'Removing --restore or --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci flags from scripts/enable-required-check.sh.' These are operationally depended upon via ADOPT-001 §12.8 break-glass Gate 1 and should carry the same protection as the original flags."},{"id":"CG-MIN-005","severity":"MIN","claim":"CASCADE-PR-BODY.md template (as emitted by scaffold-downstream.sh) does not include an explicit invariant-1 consent-surface statement ('by merging this PR, the adopter consents to adding the SCP federation primitive required-check gate') nor an invariant-3 additive-only disclosure ('this PR adds only new files; nothing in your repo is modified or deleted'). Plan-doc §5.2(1) lists the PR body template's required content; §5.2 invariants 1 and 3 are about the adopter reviewer's awareness.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh lines 163-175 emit CASCADE-PR-BODY.md with four paragraphs: cost estimate (T-024-09), bus-factor-1 disclosure (invariant 9), version-skew reference (T-024-04 + D-036), and scorecard-emit opt-in (invariant 5). No paragraph explicitly states: (a) 'this PR is the opt-in consent surface per plan-doc invariant 1' or (b) 'no existing files in this repo are modified by this PR — only policy-check-wrapper.yml is added (invariant 3)'. Review instructions invariant 1 question: 'does scaffolder name the consent surface (adopter wrapper PR) in CASCADE-PR-BODY.md template? Yes/no.' Answer is borderline: the PR implicitly IS the consent surface but does not name itself as such. Invariant 3 question: 'does CASCADE-PR-BODY.md template surface this expectation explicitly?' No.","impact":"An adopter-side reviewer reading the PR body sees what is being added (cost, bus-factor-1, version-skew, scorecard-emit) but does not see a statement like 'nothing else in your repo is touched' or 'merging this is your opt-in decision.' This could lead adopter reviewers to wonder what else might have changed and require additional investigation, or to miss that this is a governance opt-in decision point (not just a tooling addition).","mitigation":"Add two sentences to CASCADE-PR-BODY.md template: (1) after the cost paragraph, add: 'This PR is purely additive — only .github/workflows/policy-check-wrapper.yml is added; no existing files are modified or deleted (per WP-SCP-024 plan-doc invariant 3).' (2) at the top or bottom of the body, add: 'By merging this PR the adopter consents to enabling the SCP federation primitive required-check on the default branch (WP-SCP-024 plan-doc invariant 1 — consent surface).'"},{"id":"CG-MIN-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh has no test case for cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump where branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified. The expected failure in cases 5-8 is the STATUS.md TF row check, not the log-modified check. There is no case with cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump AND branch-protection-log.md unmodified. check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 183-185: for onboarded-operator-bump, the first check is '[ branch_log_modified -eq 1 ] || die ERROR'. This check path is untested.","impact":"A slice that declares cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump but forgets to include the invocation log entry would pass all existing tests but should fail CI. The unmodified-log check in onboarded-operator-bump mode (the most likely operator error) has no test coverage.","mitigation":"Add a case where cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump, STATUS.md has a valid TF row, but branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified.
